test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Who presented the Digital Payments Award 2024-25 to India Post Payments Bank for its efforts in digital inclusion?

options.text: Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman and Shri Pankaj Chaudhary
Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw and Dr. Bhagwat Karad
Smt. Anupriya Patel and Shri Rajeev Chandrasekhar
Shri Dharmendra Pradhan and Shri Hardeep Singh Puri

solution:
The correct answer is __**Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman and Shri Pankaj Chaudhary**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Digital Payments Award 2024-25** was presented to recognize and celebrate the outstanding contributions of various institutions toward building a **robust digital payment ecosystem** in India.

• **India Post Payments Bank (IPPB)** was specifically honored for its significant impact on **digital inclusion**, bridging the financial gap between urban and rural populations through its technology-driven model.

• The award was presented by the **Union Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs**, **Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman**, and the **Minister of State for Finance**, **Shri Pankaj Chaudhary**, during a high-profile event focused on the progress of the **Digital India** initiative.

• IPPB has successfully leveraged the **India Post** network, which consists of over **1,55,000 access points**, to deliver secure and efficient **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** services and **Unified Payments Interface (UPI)** solutions to the doorstep of citizens.

• The bank has played a critical role in enhancing **financial literacy** and onboarding millions of first-time digital users onto the **formal banking system** using biometric-based authentication.

 **Additional Information__**

• **India Post Payments Bank (IPPB)**:

• Launched on **September 1, 2018**, it is a 100% government-owned entity under the **Department of Posts**, **Ministry of Communications**.

• Its core philosophy is based on the **Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS)**, allowing for **interoperable** banking transactions without the need for physical debit cards or smartphones.

• It manages more than **8 crore accounts**, primarily focusing on **unbanked** segments, small businesses, and migrant laborers.

• **Financial Inclusion Framework**:

• The **Ministry of Finance** and the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** utilize the **Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index)** to monitor the penetration and quality of financial services across the country.

• The **Digital Payments Index (DPI)** is another tool used to measure the growth of digital transactions, which has seen a multi-fold increase due to the success of **UPI** and **NPCI** initiatives.
